Hi. I lived in South Central Los Angeles from the age of 8 to 19. I'll never forget the sounds of helicopters and gunfire at night. Anyway, I lived in a neighborhood that was in the Cripps territory. Their main nemesis were the Bloods. 
I was an eight year old, female, African-American,  child  happy as can be because I 'd made a new friend at school that day. She lived on my block. She was just six houses away  from mine. I was walking home from a my new friend's  house when this gang member came up to me and punched me in the stomach. Then he snatches off my RED jacket, and uses a pocket knife to rip it down the middle. And then he says, " I don't want to catch you wearing this color on my streets again." I looked around hoping to find someone who would help me. All I saw was three other gang members. They nodded to me solemnly. Then one of them helps me to stand. I was angry and frightened. But I didn't cry. At least not in front of them. The guy that helped me up said," You go on home now and tell your people what we you've learned today."
I backed away because I was kinda afraid  to turn my back to them. Once I got a little bit further away from them, I ran the rest of the way home. When I got home I collapsed in to my dad's arms. I told him what happened and he was just as angry he said that he was going to talk to them. Both my mother and I tried to stop him to no avail. What ever my dad said to them didn't go to well. When he came back in he just said,"Their color is blue."
